newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr rise to 125 yen excessive--Japan business head.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rise to 125 yen excessive--Japan business head.

text.p: The dollar's rise to 125 yen is excessive, and wild fluctuations in foreign exchange rates are not favourable for the Japanese economy, Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of the Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren), said on Monday.
"Exchange rates should reflect a country's economic fundamentals. Wild fluctuations are not favourable for the economy," Toyoda said.
"I think the dollar's rise to 125 yen is excessive... A desirable level is between 110 and 120 yen."
The dollar briefly rose to a 50-month high of 125 yen in Tokyo trading on Monday afternoon.
Toyoda also said he does not expect Japan's trade surplus to rise substantially as Japanese companies have shifted production abroad and Japan is promoting expansion of imports.
He said the increase in Japan's consumption tax from April 1 this year seemed to be having only a limited impact on the nation's economy.
"I think this is because the Japanese economy is back on its feet," he added.
